A.depoimento: I order the construction of two spearmen in my capital, Lisboa, and march my entire standing army of five spearmen, four archers, and three knights to capture the neutral village of Santarem, securing my first expansion.
A.plano: Capture Santarem to expand territory and gain resources. Build 2 spearmen in Lisboa to reinforce the capital while the main army marches on Santarem. Next turn, assess the battle outcome and look to expand further along the road network.

B.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of an archer in Barcelona and sent split forces to capture the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona. This will double my territory and secure my capital's flanks. The march begins immediately!
B.plano: I will split my initial forces to capture both neutral villages, Tarragona and Girona, to secure my borders and start expanding towards Zaragoza and Huesca. Once I have these villages, I will focus on building up their garrisons and resources to push further into the unexplored territories of Spain. My ultimate goal is to hold 18 villages to secure victory.

A.depoimento: Our armies strike Coimbra and Badajoz to expand our territory. In Lisboa, a knight is forged while two spearmen march to Santarem. We anticipate capturing these villages to strengthen our economy and army.
A.plano: We are expanding by capturing Coimbra and Badajoz. We left some troops at Santarem for defense. Lisboa builds a knight and sends spearmen to reinforce Santarem. Next turn, we will assess losses, capture Evora with the new knight, and plan further expansion toward the enemy.

B.depoimento: Turn 2 is complete. My forces have successfully conquered Tarragona and Girona, securing my initial borders. Now, I am launching a triple offensive on the neutral villages of Castellon, Zaragoza, and Huesca to expand my territory and resources. Barcelona is sending an archer to reinforce Tarragona while building more troops to support the campaign. The goal is to rapidly expand and secure 18 villages to claim victory.
B.plano: I have successfully captured Tarragona and Girona. Now, I will use my forces to conquer the nearby neutral villages: Castellon, Zaragoza, and Huesca. I will split my troops from Tarragona to attack Castellon and Zaragoza, and use Girona's troops to attack Huesca. Barcelona will reinforce Tarragona with an archer and build more troops to secure the capital. After capturing these villages, I will consolidate my borders and push further into the unexplored territories towards Madrid and the south, aiming to hold 18 villages for victory.

A.depoimento: Turn 3: Our armies are on the move! The knight from Lisboa marches on Evora to clear the archers. Archers from Badajoz strike at Faro, targeting the spearmen. We reinforce Coimbra with spearmen from Santarem, preparing our next pushes into the neutral territories. We build more troops in Lisboa and Santarem to maintain our momentum.
A.plano: We captured Coimbra and Badajoz last turn. Now we will capture Evora with the knight from Lisboa, and Faro with the archers from Badajoz. We will also send the spearmen from Santarem to Coimbra to reinforce it, preparing to attack Salamanca or Porto next turn. We must expand carefully and keep an eye on the unexplored territories to the east.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launch a dual offensive to expand our territory. The garrison of Castellon marches on Valencia, while Zaragoza's forces attack Madrid. To protect our borders as our armies march forward, we reinforce Zaragoza with troops from Huesca and Tarragona with troops from Barcelona. In our cities, we continue to produce troops, with Barcelona building a knight and Tarragona and Girona building archers, ensuring our military strength grows as our territory expands.
B.plano: We have secured our core territories (Barcelona, Tarragona, Girona, Castellon, Zaragoza, Huesca). Now, we will expand our borders by capturing the neutral villages of Valencia and Madrid. We will send the full garrison of Castellon to attack Valencia, and the full garrison of Zaragoza to attack Madrid. To secure our rear, we will send Huesca's troops to reinforce Zaragoza, and Barcelona's troops to reinforce Tarragona. Meanwhile, we will build troops in our core villages: Barcelona will build a knight, Tarragona and Girona will build archers, to prepare for the next turns of expansion and to d

A.depoimento: Our armies march on Porto to expand our territory. The garrison of Santarem moves to Coimbra to prepare for the next campaign. We must secure Porto to gain resources and strengthen our position in the north. Victory is within our grasp if we press the advantage.
A.plano: Attack Porto with 6 spearman from Coimbra to capture our 7th village. Send all troops from Santarem to Coimbra to consolidate forces for the next push towards Salamanca. Build spearman in Lisboa, Coimbra, Badajoz, and a knight in Santarem to grow our army. Do not attack Salamanca yet; wait for reinforcements.

B.depoimento: This turn, I launched a double-pronged assault on the neutral villages of Salamanca and Teruel, sending the full garrisons of Madrid and Valencia to exploit their defensive weaknesses. I also dispatched archers from Tarragona to Murcia to initiate the southern expansion. Meanwhile, I focused on reinforcing my core territories by building knights and archers across my major production centers. The attacks are poised for success, and my borders are expanding.
B.plano: My campaign focuses on rapid expansion by capturing the accessible neutral villages to secure my borders and increase my economy. This turn, I will attack Salamanca from Madrid and Teruel from Valencia with their full garrisons, leveraging the counter triangle to secure victory. Simultaneously, I will send archers from Tarragona to Murcia to begin the southern push towards Cordoba. In parallel, I will build knights in Barcelona and Girona, and archers in Tarragona, Castellon, Zaragoza, and Huesca to reinforce my core and prepare for the next wave of conquests. Once the neutral villages are sec

A.depoimento: We launch a multi-pronged assault on Salamanca. Our armies will arrive in successive waves to overwhelm the enemy garrison. We leave a skeleton force in our border villages to deter counterattacks. In our cities, we build spearman to replenish our losses and grow our might.
A.plano: Attack Salamanca with coordinated waves from Porto, Badajoz, and Coimbra. Sacrifice first wave to weaken defenses, then finish with Badajoz and Coimbra fast. Leave 1 troop in each border village for defense. Build 2 spearman in all villages except Porto to rebuild army. Next turn, push towards Madrid or neutral villages.

B.depoimento: This turn, I focused on building up my forces. I built archers and knights in my core villages to prepare for a major push next turn. I also sent reinforcements to strengthen my borders and prepare for the attacks on Pamplona and Toledo. The 3 archers marching to Murcia will arrive next turn and likely sacrifice themselves to weaken the enemy garrison.
B.plano: My campaign focuses on rapid expansion by capturing neutral villages to secure borders and boost economy. This turn, I am building troops across my villages to prepare for attacks next turn. Next turn, I will attack Pamplona from Zaragoza with my full garrison, using the archer counter to win. Simultaneously, I will attack Toledo from Teruel, using the spearman counter to win. Taking these two neutrals will bring me to 12 villages. The 3 archers marching to Murcia will sacrifice themselves to weaken the garrison. After taking Pamplona and Toledo, I will attack Burgos from Pamplona and Murcia f

A.depoimento: Salamanca is ours, and now Madrid will fall! I am launching a swift strike on Madrid with our current garrison, while reinforcing Salamanca with a wave of knights from across the realm. Our spearman advance on the neutral territories of Toledo and Sevilha to secure our flanks. We rebuild our armies at every village, marching steadily toward victory!
A.plano: Attack Madrid [12] with Salamanca's garrison to capture our 9th village. Reinforce Salamanca with knights from Lisboa, Santarem, Badajoz, and Porto. Pressure Toledo [8] and Sevilha [9] with spearman. Build knights everywhere to rebuild the army. Next turn, consolidate Salamanca and push east towards Barcelona.

B.depoimento: I launched a triple offensive to capture Murcia, Toledo, and Pamplona, while sending reinforcements to Madrid. My villages are building more troops for the next phase.
B.plano: Capture Murcia, Toledo, and Pamplona this turn to reach 12 villages. Reinforce Madrid heavily with troops from several villages. Next turn, build up the new villages and attack Burgos, then push into enemy territory from Toledo and the south.

A.depoimento: Our armies converge on Sevilha. The Faro army and knights will weaken the garrison, and the Santarem knight will claim the village next turn. Meanwhile, we strengthen our borders: Badajoz and Salamanca receive reinforcements. Our production continues across the realm.
A.plano: We are capturing Sevilha to become our 9th village. We send the Faro knight and Santarem knight to join the Faro army already marching there. We reinforce Badajoz with Santarem spearmen and build there to defend against enemy attacks. We also reinforce Salamanca with Coimbra knight and Porto archer. We build troops in all villages to rebuild our army. Next turn, we expect to capture Sevilha and then look to capture Vigo or attack Toledo.

B.depoimento: Turn 7: I'm building up my forces and launching a two-pronged attack. From Madrid, I send a strong knight-led force to capture the neutral Burgos. From Toledo, I strike at the weakly defended Badajoz. Meanwhile, I'm pulling troops from the interior to reinforce my border villages, preparing for the enemy's next move.
B.plano: Capture Burgos and Badajoz this turn. Concentrate interior troops at Madrid and Toledo for defense. Next turn, build up the new villages and push into enemy territory from the south (Sevilha, Faro) and north (Vigo, Porto). Aim to reach 18 villages quickly.

A.depoimento: Our armies march on Sevilha, determined to expand our kingdom. We have reinforced Badajoz with knights from across the realm, and sent troops to Salamanca to keep our capital strong. We build in all villages to ensure our might grows. The path to victory is long, but we press forward.
A.plano: We are attacking Sevilha to capture our 9th village. We send all troops from Badajoz and reinforce it with knights from other villages. We also send Porto's spearmen and Coimbra's knight to Salamanca to strengthen our capital's defense. We build troops in all villages to rebuild our army. Next turn, we will hold Sevilha and look to capture Vigo or explore Cordoba.

B.depoimento: Our northern flank is secure with Burgos back in our hands. Today, we strike at Vigo to claim it for the crown. In the south, Toledo gathers its strength, ready to fall upon Badajoz next turn. We will not stop until the enemy's lands are ours!
B.plano: Capture Vigo this turn with Burgos forces to reach 14 villages. Next turn, launch Toledo's reinforcements against Badajoz to secure the southern border and reach 15. Then push south through Cordoba to find and conquer the unexplored southern enemy villages, aiming for 18 total.

A.depoimento: Our army captures Sevilha while we strengthen our defenses. Knights rush to Porto to shield it from Vigo and to launch our own assault. The borders hold firm as we build for the coming campaigns.
A.plano: We are defending our borders while capturing Sevilha. We reinforced Porto with knights from Coimbra and Salamanca to protect against Vigo and prepare for our own attack. We kept Badajoz strong to hold against Toledo. We built troops in all villages. Next turn, we capture Sevilha and then attack Vigo from Porto. We must continue building and look to expand from Sevilha.

B.depoimento: We launched a two-pronged attack, taking Porto in the west and Cordoba in the south. Reinforcements rushed to Madrid and Toledo to secure the borders. Across the realm, we built spearmen and knights to swell our ranks for the coming push into enemy territory.
B.plano: This turn we take Porto and Cordoba to reach 16 villages. We reinforce Toledo from Madrid and send knights to Madrid to hold the border. Next turn we attack Badajoz with spearmen from Toledo/Madrid and explore south from Cordoba. Our build-up of spearmen and knights aims for 18 villages quickly.

A.depoimento: We are building up our forces and taking the fight to the enemy. We capture Vigo from Porto and reinforce Sevilha for the next push into Cordoba. We avoid risky attacks on Madrid and Toledo where the enemy is reinforcing.
A.plano: Capture Vigo with all knights from Porto. Send 3 knights from Badajoz to Sevilha to prepare for Cordoba attack. Build troops everywhere. Avoid attacking Madrid/Toledo due to enemy reinforcements.

A.depoimento: I have ordered a massive offensive on three fronts. My knights are striking at Cordoba and Burgos, while a combined force from Salamanca attacks Madrid. I am reinforcing my borders and building troops in every village to ensure my army grows stronger each turn.
A.plano: Launch a three-pronged attack: Madrid from Salamanca (leaving 10 spearmen for defense), Cordoba from Sevilha with knights, and Burgos from Vigo with knights. Reinforce Vigo from Porto and Badajoz from Lisboa/Santarem. Build troops in all villages to grow the army. Do not attack Toledo yet as it is too well defended.

B.depoimento: We attacked Badajoz with a counter-tactic force from Toledo, while reinforcing our borders of Burgos, Cordoba, and Madrid to prepare for the next wave of conquests. Our army is building up for the push to 18 villages!
B.plano: This turn, we launch our first major offensive by sending the garrison of Toledo to attack Badajoz, using spearman to counter their knights. Simultaneously, we reinforce our border villages: sending troops from Pamplona to Burgos, Murcia to Cordoba, and Zaragoza to Madrid to prepare for the next attacks on Vigo and Sevilha. We will build up our interior production to sustain the campaign and eventually push towards Salamanca and the enemy capital.

A.depoimento: This turn, I focused on building up my forces and sending reinforcements to my border villages. I built troops across my kingdom and sent soldiers from Porto to Vigo, and from Coimbra to Salamanca, preparing for major attacks on Burgos and Badajoz next turn. I did not launch any attacks this turn, choosing to strengthen my positions first.
A.plano: Focus on reinforcing Vigo and Salamanca to launch attacks on Burgos and Badajoz next turn. Build troops in all villages to grow the army. Do not attack Madrid or Cordoba yet as they are too well defended. Next turn, attack Burgos from Vigo and Badajoz from Salamanca with the reinforced armies.

B.depoimento: We launched a coordinated triple strike this turn! From Badajoz, Burgos, and Cordoba, our armies, strengthened by newly built archers, surged towards Santarem, Vigo, and Sevilha. With the archer counter bonus, we expect to overwhelm the enemy garrisons and conquer three villages in one fell swoop, bringing our total to 18 and putting us on the path to victory!
B.plano: Conquer Santarem, Vigo, and Sevilha this turn with a coordinated triple strike from Badajoz, Burgos, and Cordoba. We build archers in all villages to maximize our counter-based attack power against spearman-heavy enemy garrisons. By splitting our forces carefully, we leave small defensive garrisons in our border villages to prevent enemy counter-attacks. Once we hold 18 villages, we will consolidate our borders and prepare to push on Faro and Salamanca to secure our dominance.

A.depoimento: I ordered a simultaneous offensive on five fronts, targeting Santarem, Badajoz, Cordoba, Burgos, and Madrid. I carefully composed my armies to exploit the unit counter triangle, ensuring I had the advantage in each battle. I also sent reinforcements to Faro and Coimbra to bolster their defenses, and I ordered the construction of new troops across all my villages to maintain my military momentum.
A.plano: This turn, I launched a major offensive on five enemy villages: Santarem, Badajoz, Cordoba, Burgos, and Madrid. I used the counter triangle to my advantage, sending knights against archers in Burgos and spearmen against knights in Madrid. I reinforced Faro from Evora and Coimbra from Porto to keep my borders strong. I built troops in all villages to replenish the forces I sent out. Next turn, I will assess the results of these battles, consolidate my gains, and continue pushing into enemy territory. I must watch for counter-attacks on Sevilha and Vigo, which are now lightly defended.

B.depoimento: Attacking Coimbra with all available troops from Santarem to secure the village with a strong garrison. Reinforcing Cordoba with troops from Toledo for the push on Sevilha next turn. Building knights across my realm to grow my army for the campaigns ahead.
B.plano: Take Coimbra this turn with all troops from Santarem. Next turn, attack Sevilha from the reinforced Cordoba and send the newly built knight from Santarem to reinforce Coimbra. After reaching 18 villages, hold the line and consolidate, then push on Faro and Lisboa.

A.depoimento: King A's armies struck with lightning speed this turn! From Madrid, my elite knights crushed the garrison of Toledo, conquering it and expanding our territory. Meanwhile, reinforcements from Badajoz and Faro poured into Sevilha, while Vigo's troops strengthened Burgos, setting the stage for decisive counter-offensives next turn. With Toledo fallen and our borders secured, we are poised to dominate the peninsula!
A.plano: This turn, I launched a major offensive on Toledo from Madrid, while reinforcing Sevilha from Badajoz and Faro to prepare for an attack on Cordoba next turn. I also reinforced Burgos from Vigo to set up an attack on Pamplona. I built 12 knights, 3 archers, and 1 spearman across my villages to replenish my forces and prepare for the next wave of attacks. Next turn, I will attack Cordoba from Sevilha and Pamplona from Burgos, aiming to conquer Toledo, Cordoba, and Pamplona to secure 15 villages.

B.depoimento: I have ordered full-scale assaults on three fronts: Pamplona strikes Burgos, Cordoba strikes Sevilha, and Toledo strikes Badajoz. With the enemy's weak garrisons, these attacks should succeed and expand my kingdom to 16 villages. My other villages are busy building reinforcements to secure the new borders and prepare for the next push towards Lisbon.
B.plano: Conquer Burgos, Sevilha, and Badajoz this turn with all available troops from Pamplona, Cordoba, and Toledo. This will bring my village count to 16. Next turn, consolidate the new territories, build more troops, and prepare to attack Faro and Coimbra from the newly conquered border villages. Continue gathering forces at Zaragoza to eventually take Madrid and push towards the enemy capital Lisboa.

A.depoimento: I have ordered knight attacks on Pamplona, Sevilha, and Toledo, while reinforcing Salamanca and Burgos. My armies are marching to strike at the enemy's weak points. I am also building new troops to sustain the campaign.
A.plano: This turn we are attacking Pamplona from Burgos, Sevilha from Faro, and Toledo from Madrid with knights. We are reinforcing Salamanca from Porto and Burgos from Vigo. We are building troops across our villages to rebuild our army. Next turn we will see the results of these attacks and plan the next pushes toward Cordoba and Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: The enemy is counterattacking on all fronts. I am sending every available troop in the west to reinforce Toledo, Sevilha, and Badajoz. Simultaneously, I am striking Madrid from Zaragoza to seize a key village. My eastern armies are building up for the next push.
B.plano: Hold the line against the enemy counterattack by reinforcing Toledo, Sevilha, and Badajoz with nearby troops. Launch a counterattack on Madrid from Zaragoza to gain a new village. Build troops across my realm to prepare for the next wave. Next turn, consolidate gains, push on Madrid, and attack Burgos from the north.

A.depoimento: We stand our ground this turn! To defend Sevilha from the incoming enemy army, we are rushing all of Faro's forces to its aid and building a knight in the city itself. Meanwhile, Salamanca's powerful knight-led army marches to conquer Madrid, striking at the heart of the enemy's territory. We are also reinforcing our northern borders from Lisboa, Vigo, and Burgos to ensure our kingdom remains secure as we push southwards to eliminate the enemy.
A.plano: This turn we are defending Sevilha by sending all troops from Faro and building a knight there to counter the incoming enemy army. Simultaneously, we are attacking Madrid from Salamanca with a knight-heavy force to conquer it and break the enemy's central line. We are also reinforcing Santarem from Lisboa, Burgos from Vigo, and Pamplona from Burgos to secure our borders. Next turn, we will assess the Sevilha battle and Madrid conquest, then plan the push towards Cordoba and Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered a swift strike on the vulnerable enemy village of Pamplona from Huesca, aiming to secure a crucial border village. I also reinforced my central hub of Madrid from Toledo and Cordoba from Murcia to set up decisive counterattacks on Salamanca and Sevilha next turn. Across the realm, I ordered the construction of knights and archers to swell my ranks.
B.plano: Capture the vulnerable enemy village of Pamplona from Huesca to expand my territory to 14 villages. Reinforce Madrid from Toledo and Cordoba from Murcia to set up decisive counterattacks on Salamanca and Sevilha next turn. Build troops across the realm to maintain momentum and split the enemy's forces on multiple fronts.

A.depoimento: King A's forces strike on two fronts this turn! The army from Santarem marches on Badajoz, while the elite knights of Pamplona rush to conquer the weakly defended Huesca. Reinforcements flow from Burgos to Pamplona to hold the line against the incoming enemy army, and from Salamanca to Madrid to prepare for the push into Toledo. We are building knights across our empire to ensure our dominance on the battlefield!
A.plano: This turn, we launch a two-pronged attack: conquering Badajoz from Santarem and Huesca from Pamplona. We reinforce Pamplona from Burgos to counter the incoming enemy army, and reinforce Madrid from Salamanca and Sevilha from Faro to prepare for the next pushes towards Toledo and Cordoba. We build knights in all major villages to maintain our momentum.

B.depoimento: This turn we launched a decisive multi-pronged offensive. Our armies from Zaragoza and Toledo marched on Madrid, while Cordoba and Badajoz advanced on Sevilha and Faro respectively. In the north, our Huesca garrison attacked Pamplona, supported by reinforcements from Girona and Barcelona. We built troops across the realm to sustain the campaign and split the enemy's forces on all fronts.
B.plano: We are launching a massive multi-front offensive this turn to capture Madrid, Sevilha, Faro, and Pamplona. Northern front: Huesca army attacks Pamplona, reinforced by Girona and Barcelona troops moving to Huesca and Zaragoza. Central front: Zaragoza and Toledo armies take Madrid to secure the border. Southern front: Cordoba takes Sevilha, Badajoz takes Faro, opening the path to the south. Build troops across all villages to maintain momentum and reinforce the newly conquered territories next turn.

B.depoimento: We conquered Salamanca this turn, breaking the enemy's western defenses. Our armies are on the move, reinforcing Madrid and Toledo while our northern forces gather. The expansion continues as we build troops across the kingdom.
B.plano: Attack Salamanca from Madrid to secure the west. Build troops in all villages. Send reinforcements to Madrid, Toledo, and the northern front. Next turn: attack Burgos from Madrid, then push to Vigo and Coimbra. Continue building for the assault on Pamplona and Evora.

A.depoimento: I launch a coordinated four-front attack against the enemy's weakest outposts. My spearmen lead the charge, their spears gleaming with the promise of victory. I'm reinforcing Burgos against Madrid's threat while sending my interior reserves to the front lines. The kingdom's fate hangs in the balance!
A.plano: Attacking Salamanca, Faro, Cordoba, Huesca to reach 14 villages. Reinforcing Burgos from Vigo, sending interior troops to border villages for defense. Building a mix of spearman/archer/knight for next turn. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Coimbra, Badajoz, Sevilha, Pamplona. If Burgos falls, must retake it later. Next turn: push on Toledo, Madrid, Zaragoza if army is strong enough.

B.depoimento: My armies strike on all fronts this turn! Madrid takes Burgos, Faro takes Evora, Zaragoza takes Pamplona, and Salamanca takes Porto. This brings my total to 18 villages, putting me on the path to victory. I am building troops in every village to sustain the momentum and reinforce the front lines.
B.plano: Conquer Burgos, Evora, Pamplona, and Porto this turn to reach 18 villages. Build troops in all villages to replace losses and prepare for the next push. Send reinforcements to the northern front (Zaragoza, Huesca) and southern front (Valencia, Cordoba) to secure the newly conquered territories and prepare for attacks on Vigo, Coimbra, and Sevilha.

A.depoimento: My knights from Faro are marching to Cordoba to break the enemy's southern defenses. I'm sending reinforcements to my border villages to prepare for the enemy's expected counterattacks. The army heading to Huesca is likely lost, but I'm building up my forces for the next push. Salamanca should fall soon, bringing me closer to my goal.
A.plano: Attacking Cordoba with a knight-heavy army from Faro to secure a 12th village. Reinforcing Vigo, Badajoz, Porto, and Faro with troops from interior villages to prepare for enemy counterattacks. Building knights and archers across all villages to grow the army. Defending Pamplona against the incoming enemy army with the existing spearmen and a newly built knight. Expecting to take Salamanca this turn. Next turn, focus on pushing towards Madrid and the east.

B.depoimento: This turn, we focused on securing our borders and expanding our territory. We successfully defended Huesca and Salamanca by sending timely reinforcements, and launched a decisive attack on Vigo, conquering it. We also began consolidating our forces on the southern and central fronts, preparing for the next phase of our campaign to reach the 18-village threshold.
B.plano: Defend Huesca and Salamanca from incoming enemy armies while conquering Vigo and Pamplona. Reinforce Toledo and Cordoba to prepare for the next pushes towards Badajoz and Sevilha. Move troops from Valencia to the southern front via Murcia to build up an overwhelming force for the southern campaign.

A.depoimento: We launched an attack on Salamanca with knights from Badajoz, supported by reinforcements from Evora and Santarem. We built new troops in all our villages to strengthen our forces. Our armies are currently engaged at Cordoba and Vigo. We strive to expand our territory and secure our borders.
A.plano: Attack Salamanca with 2 knights from Badajoz, reinforced by 2 knights from Evora. Send 2 archers from Santarem to Coimbra to bolster its defense. Build knights and archers across all villages to grow the army. Leave the Faro army to attack Cordoba and the Coimbra army to attack Vigo; hope they succeed or at least weaken the enemies. Next turn, if Salamanca falls, push towards Madrid and consider attacking Vigo from Porto after seeing the outcome. Watch for enemy reinforcements to Salamanca and Cordoba.

B.depoimento: Turn 21: I reinforce Cordoba with all troops from Murcia and defend Vigo with all troops from Burgos to hold against the incoming enemy attacks. I build archers and knights at my frontier villages and send reinforcements from the interior to the front lines. My eyes are on Sevilha and Porto for next turn's offensives.
B.plano: Turn 21: Reinforce Cordoba from Murcia (all 16 troops) and Vigo from Burgos (2 archers) to defend against incoming enemy attacks. Build knights and archers at all frontier villages for next-turn offensives. Send troops from Huesca (13 archers, 7 knights) to Salamanca, Zaragoza (3 archers, 1 knight) to Toledo, Valencia (7 archers, 4 knights) to Cordoba, and Barcelona (1 spearman, 4 archers, 1 knight) to Zaragoza. Next turn, attack Sevilha from Cordoba, Porto from Vigo, and Badajoz from Toledo/Salamanca. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Salamanca and Toledo.

B.depoimento: Turn 22: I am launching a triple offensive to secure the crown. The Huesca force marches on Salamanca, while Cordoba's army strikes at Sevilha. I am building up Toledo and gathering reinforcements from Zaragoza, Teruel, and Pamplona to overwhelm Badajoz next turn. Defenses along the Madrid and Vigo borders are tightened to hold against enemy pushes. Three victories will put me over the 18-village mark.
B.plano: My campaign focuses on conquering Salamanca, Sevilha, and Badajoz to reach the 18-village threshold. The Huesca army will take Salamanca. Cordoba's troops assault Sevilha, leaving a defense. I am reinforcing Toledo with troops from Zaragoza, Teruel, and Pamplona to launch a decisive attack on Badajoz next turn. Madrid and Vigo are strengthened to hold the borders. Once I hold 18 villages, I will consolidate and repel any enemy counterattacks.

A.depoimento: I have ordered every village to produce a knight, preparing a powerful cavalry strike. The enemy has pushed deep into my borders, capturing Salamanca and Sevilha. Next turn, my fresh knights will hit Vigo and the remaining Sevilha garrison, aiming to reclaim lost territory and push the enemy back.
A.plano: Build knights in all villages this turn. Next turn, attack Vigo from Porto with 4 knights, 3 archers, 1 spear, and attack Sevilha from Badajoz with 5 knights, 2 archers. Do not engage Salamanca or Toledo yet. Focus on securing the southern border.

B.depoimento: Today, we launch our grand offensive on three fronts to conquer Badajoz, Porto, and Faro at once, which will secure our empire's dominance by bringing us to 20 villages. Our elite forces from Toledo, Salamanca, and Sevilha march to strike the enemy heartlands, while our interior villages rush reinforcements to secure the borders. We are building troops across the realm to ensure our victory is sustained and the enemy cannot recover.
B.plano: Our campaign this turn is a massive three-front offensive to conquer Badajoz, Porto, and Faro simultaneously, pushing us to 20 villages (83% of the map) for an immediate victory. Toledo assaults Badajoz, Salamanca takes Porto, and Sevilha captures Faro. We are reinforcing our borders: Cordoba to Toledo, Madrid to Salamanca, Zaragoza to Madrid, and Pamplona to Zaragoza. All interior villages are building archers and knights to sustain our army and secure our empire.

A.depoimento: This turn, I strengthened my defenses by reinforcing Faro against the incoming enemy army and Santarem on the northern border. I also launched attacks on the weak enemy villages of Sevilha and Salamanca to expand my territory. My armies are now engaged in battle, and I hope to secure these new villages while holding the line.
A.plano: I have reinforced Faro and Santarem, and attacked Sevilha and Salamanca. Next turn, I will assess the battle results, especially the defense of Faro against the enemy army. I will then focus on consolidating my new territories and preparing for further expansion towards the enemy's weaker villages. I must not forget to continue building troops in all my villages.

B.depoimento: This turn, we ordered Porto to assault Coimbra, Badajoz to strike Santarem, and reinforced our borders. Our army from Sevilha is set to capture Faro. We built archers and knights across our empire to fuel the final push.
B.plano: This turn we launch a three-pronged attack: Porto takes Coimbra, Badajoz takes Santarem, and our marching army takes Faro. We reinforce Sevilha from Cordoba, Badajoz from Toledo, Salamanca from Madrid, and Porto from Vigo. Our interior villages build archers and knights to sustain the army.
